sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closest to A. darwini; it differs in the deeper head with a more rounded vertex, the shorter and narrower labrum, the similarly shaped mandibles whose tooth is slightly hooked, and the usually distinctly broader gula.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Not recorded in the original (Not known).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head deeper, the vertex more rounded; labrum shorter and narrower; mandibles similar in shape to those of A. darwini, but the mandibular tooth slightly hooked. Gula usually distinctly broader: in the very smallest individuals 0.33 mm wide at the narrowest point, in ordinary and large individuals about 0.40 mm; the maximum width of the gula in A. darwini is 0.33 mm. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 the smallest, often closely fused with segment 4; segment 5 shorter than segments 4 and 6; or segment 4 sometimes smaller than segment 3, and segments 3 and 5 about equal. Measurements (smallest and largest individuals of the type series): total length 4.00—5.50 mm, head length (including mandibles) 1.98—2.49 mm, head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.02—1.39 mm, head length (to apex of labrum) 1.14—1.90 mm, head width 1.04—1.39 mm, pronotum length 0.33—0.42 mm, width 0.62—0.84 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original describes only the soldier, records the alate as Not known and does not describe the worker (the type series includes workers but there is no morphological account). OCR problems: the heading and genus name read "Eamitermes" (Hamitermes); the gula width "o.l+o" is defective and, from the letter shapes and the context, is read as 0.40 mm, which remains doubtful; the head length (to apex of labrum) "1.1+4 - 1.90" is recorded as 1.14—1.90; "sth" is 5th. The original states that the measurements are those of the smallest and largest individuals of the type series, most specimens being slightly below the maximum. The type locality Queensland: Rollingstone agrees with the checklist.
